To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expansion of dystrophin-positive revertant fibers (a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophies) depends on the mutation type and age in mdx and Mdx52 mice.
the number of RF clusters in mdx mice was significantly higher compared to that in mdx52 mice, which suggests that the type of mutation in the dystrophin gene is a major factor in RF expansion.

the number of RF clusters is higher in mdx than in mdx52 mice and increases with age in mdx but not in mdx52, whereas the number of centrally-nucleated fibers and embryonmyosin heavy chain (EMHCh)-positive fibers decrease with age in both strains.
